correctness.rationale: PASS. An affine map of the ellipse to the unit circle preserves area order and reduces a convex n-gon to positive cyclic angular gaps with sum 2π. At an area maximum, adjusting any single vertex forces its adjacent gaps equal by a strict cosine maximum on their fixed interval; hence all gaps 2π/n and the family is exhaustive. Direct chord subtraction gives the grouped q=n/gcd(n,2) square-root sum. The Chebyshev monic product for q equally spaced phases and the Stieltjes square-root representation give F'(c)<0 and F''(c)<0 for α>β>0; z(s)>1 ensures no singularity, with finite dominated differentiated integrals at both ends. The positive increasing resolvent G yields sharp lower and upper phase-deficit constants as limits at maxima and values at minima. An independent finite geometry script checked representative direct perimeters, grouping, and orientation order; near-circular differences below double precision were excluded from sign claims. All n≥3, a>b>0 are covered by analytic proof, not by tests.
